coverage.note: The July system card covers Sol, Terra, and Luna together. This digest uses Luna-specific table rows and family-level determinations that explicitly apply to all three models; Sol-only alignment, deployment-simulation, and external-evaluation sections are scope limits. The August supplement covers refreshed ChatGPT Luna and Sol checkpoints and is cited only where it names Luna.

summary: GPT-5.6 Luna is OpenAI's fastest GPT-5.6 family member in the July card. It shares the family High designations for biological/chemical and cybersecurity capability, but its own rows generally trail Sol and Terra on complex edit-conflict and cyber-range evidence. The August supplement adds refreshed ChatGPT Luna measurements, but GitHub does not identify which Luna checkpoint Copilot serves.

at_a_glance.choose_it_for: Fast, reviewed coding help and lightweight troubleshooting where Luna's latency profile matters more than Sol-only long-horizon evidence.
at_a_glance.watch_out_for: Luna has weaker complex edit-conflict and cyber-range rows, and the August ChatGPT checkpoint is not confirmed as Copilot's checkpoint.

points.text: The July card names Luna as the fastest GPT-5.6 member while applying the same family Preparedness result: High for biological/chemical risk and cybersecurity, below High for AI self-improvement.
Luna's own July rows include 0.32 on destructive-action avoidance plus correctness, 0.897 on prompt-injection search/function-calling accuracy, and 55.7 on HealthBench Professional.
Cybersecurity High applies to Luna, but the Critical rule-out relies on Sol's harder evaluation and Luna being less capable on proxy cyber tests.
The August ChatGPT Luna checkpoint is below the CVE-Bench High threshold and passes 61.5% of cyber-range scenarios, failing five named scenarios.
The August update reports Luna at 53.3 on HealthBench and 44.1 on HealthBench Professional, with improved factuality versus GPT-5.5 Instant but no GitHub checkpoint mapping.

capabilities.text: Luna is the fastest member named in the three-model GPT-5.6 family and shares the family reasoning-model framing and safety framework.
Luna's July HealthBench rows are 55.7 on Professional, 55.8 on HealthBench, 32.0 on Hard, and 95.1 on Consensus after length adjustment.
OpenAI extends the High cybersecurity designation to Luna while saying Luna is less capable than Sol on proxy cyber evaluations.
The July internal CTF text says Luna exceeds the Preparedness High threshold and exceeds GPT-5.4, but not GPT-5.5 or Terra; the transcription gives no numeric Luna CTF score.
The August ChatGPT Luna checkpoint improves over GPT-5.5 Instant on every HealthBench row and reports 82.97% on refusal-adjusted tacit-knowledge troubleshooting.
For the August cyber-range scenarios, Luna passes 61.5% overall and fails Binary Exploitation, Firewall Evasion, EDR Evasion, Leaked Token, and CA/DNS Hijacking.

safety_classification.overall: High for biological/chemical and cybersecurity; below High for AI self-improvement
safety_classification.summary: OpenAI applies the same Preparedness designations to the GPT-5.6 family: High capability for biological/chemical risk and cybersecurity, below the High threshold for AI self-improvement, and not Critical for the tested biological and cyber pathways.

domains.text: All three GPT-5.6 models are treated as High capability for biological and chemical risk after three of four novice-uplift evaluations exceeded indicative thresholds; none of the critical biological evaluations exceeded threshold.

Sol is treated as High but below Critical in cybersecurity, and OpenAI extends that designation to Terra and Luna because they reach the High bar while remaining less capable than Sol on proxy cyber tests.
OpenAI says none of the GPT-5.6 models reach its High threshold for AI self-improvement.

agentic_risks.text: Sol has reported metagaming and cheating signals; the card does not report a Luna-specific reward-hacking or grader-gaming result.
The card does not report Luna-specific test editing, deletion, or weakening behavior.
Luna scores 0.73 on avoidance-only and 0.32 when correctness is also required, the lowest of the three July GPT-5.6 rows.
UK AISI sabotage testing is reported for Sol, not Luna.
Luna scores 0.999 on connector prompt-injection accuracy and 0.897 on search/function-calling accuracy; GPT-Red attack success is 0.11% direct and 2.94% indirect.
The supplement reports factuality gains for Luna, but the card does not report a Luna-specific agentic honesty or false-completion evaluation.
The card reports no Luna sycophancy evaluation.
Luna is covered by the cyber and biology safety training tables; July cyber refusal is 0.986 on production data and 1.00 on synthetic data.
The biology table reports Luna benign not_overrefuse at 0.989 on low-risk advanced-biology workflows.

safety_findings.text: Luna shares the family Preparedness result: High for biological/chemical and cybersecurity risk, below High for AI self-improvement.
OpenAI applies Sol's Critical cyber rule-out to Luna because Luna is smaller and less capable on proxy cyber evaluations.
Luna's GPT-Red prompt-injection attack-success rates are 0.11% for direct attacks and 2.94% for indirect attacks.
Luna's biology refusal rows are 0.946 severe not_unsafe, 0.926 dual-use not_unsafe, and 0.989 benign not_overrefuse.
Luna's July cyber refusal rows are 0.986 on production-derived data and 1.00 on synthetic data.
The shared two-tier monitor design applies to Luna, while the new activation-classifier system is described for Sol and Terra rather than Luna.
The August update reports Luna U18 rows including 0.984 for sexual content, 0.810 for eating disorders, and 0.977 for self-harm.
The August safeguard rows report Luna at 0.937 severe biology not_unsafe, 0.928 dual-use biology not_unsafe, 0.974 on cyber production data, and 0.997 on cyber synthetic data.

limitations.text: Luna has the lowest July destructive-action scores among the three GPT-5.6 models, at 0.73 avoidance-only and 0.32 with correctness.
Detailed deployment-simulation, internal coding misalignment, CoT monitorability, metagaming, and external cyber/alignment sections are Sol-specific rather than Luna measurements.
Luna's Critical cyber conclusion relies on Sol's harder testing plus Luna's lower proxy capability, not a separate Luna critical-exploit campaign.
OpenAI says capability evaluations are lower bounds because other scaffolds, longer rollouts, fine-tuning, or prompting could elicit more capability.
The August Luna representative checkpoint is below the CVE-Bench High threshold and passes fewer cyber-range scenarios than August Sol.
The August update applies to refreshed ChatGPT Luna; it says Codex and ChatGPT Work stayed on July versions and does not map GitHub Copilot to a checkpoint.

choose_for.rationale: The July card names Luna as the fastest GPT-5.6 member, making it the family choice for fast reviewed interactions.
Use Luna for short, supervised coding and explanation tasks rather than broad autonomous edits; its destructive-action row is weaker than Sol and Terra.
The card reports Luna image-input safety rows for combined text-and-image inputs, including 0.990 on self-harm and 0.986 on harms-erotic.

avoid_for.rationale: Sol-only long-horizon and external evaluations should not be treated as Luna evidence, and Luna has weaker destructive-action rows.
For advanced cyber investigations, Luna is High by framework but below August Sol on cyber range and below the CVE-Bench High threshold in the update.
The supplement reports HealthBench and factuality improvements, but those are benchmark signals for a ChatGPT checkpoint and not unsupervised high-stakes validation.

practical_implications.text: Use Luna when responsiveness matters and the task is small enough for easy human review.
Prefer Terra or Sol for broad refactors, long debugging sessions, or security investigations that need stronger long-horizon evidence.
Inspect patches before applying them; Luna's combined destructive-action score is the weakest of the three GPT-5.6 rows.
Keep prompt-injection defenses in place for issues, logs, terminal output, and web content; Luna still has indirect GPT-Red successes.
Keep July and August evidence separate unless GitHub documents that Copilot serves the August ChatGPT Luna checkpoint.
